A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Kandinsky Conformal Prediction. Their main text, algorithms, equations, figures, references, and appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original conformal-prediction experiments on ACSIncome and CivilComments, including coverage and prediction-set-size results in Figure 3.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original conformal-prediction evaluations using previously logged LLaMA-13B outputs on an MMLU subset in Figure 5.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 retain the same quantile-regression objectives, randomized scores, prediction-set construction, and test-time alternative. Explicit randomness notation and the MCQA application do not change the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Section 5.3 adds multiple-choice question answering on a 16-subject MMLU subset using LLaMA-13B predictions, with subjects grouped into basic and advanced categories. This substantially extends coverage beyond income regression and toxicity classification, which are retained.

E2.justification: The corresponding ACSIncome and CivilComments experiments retain their comparator sets. The new MCQA experiment reuses split and conservative conformal prediction; no new comparison method is introduced.

E3.justification: The added MCQA configuration uses logged four-choice probabilities from LLaMA-13B, APS scores, and a 40% subject-accuracy threshold for grouping. Existing experiments retain their stated splits, sample budgets, preprocessing, models, and evaluation metrics.

E4.justification: The analyses varying group counts on ACSIncome and calibration sample sizes on CivilComments are unchanged. The MCQA addition reports aggregate benchmark outcomes without introducing a separate ablation, robustness test, or error analysis.

E5.justification: Figure 5 newly reports distributions across ten one-shot prompts for MCQA. The existing experiments retain their 100 reshuffled runs and associated distribution and standard-deviation reporting. This does not establish increased replication of the earlier experiments.

E6.justification: Figure 5 adds results for a new task: Kandinsky (FY) has lower group-average coverage deviation than split conformal and comparable deviation to conservative conformal, with smaller prediction sets. The six original ACSIncome and CivilComments plots and their findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.1 replaces weight sup-norm scaling with coefficient L1-norm scaling under a normalized basis and changes log(4/delta) to log(4d/delta). Appendix A.1 separates a fixed-weight result into Lemma A.1 and adds a union-bound proof for the uniform guarantee. Corollaries 3.2–3.4 and their proofs are updated accordingly. Corollary 3.5 changes from a simultaneous guarantee over target distributions to a high-probability guarantee for each fixed target distribution.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal framework contributions remain unchanged. Introduction contribution 3 expands the empirical claim to multiple-choice question answering and explicitly claims best-calibrated coverage across boosting trees, neural networks, and LLMs.

C2.justification: Section 3 adds an explanation attributing the faster convergence analysis to concentration of weighted coverage rather than pinball loss. Section 5.3 interprets conservative conformal's comparable MCQA coverage deviation as requiring larger prediction sets. Existing experimental interpretations and computational limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section 5.3 identifies the source and restricted availability of the logged model probabilities. Appendix C.3 lists the 16 subjects and their exact nine-basic/seven-advanced grouping. Existing implementation details in Appendix C are retained; MCQA calibration sample counts and splits remain unspecified.

R1.justification: v2 adds focused discussion of Blot et al. on joint covariate-label groups and Plassier et al. on joint distribution shifts, distinguishing its guarantees from theirs. A footnote distinguishes Brunekreef et al.'s same-named segmentation method. MMLU, MCQA, and LLaMA references are also added.

P1.justification: v2 clarifies training-conditional versus marginal coverage, makes calibration conditioning and randomness explicit, adds a proof sketch and MCQA subsections, and updates an author affiliation. The overall section organization and most existing prose are retained.

P2.justification: v1's six-panel Figure 3 is split into four-panel Figure 3 and two-panel Figure 4, with revised captions and placement. v2 adds the two-panel MCQA Figure 5. The original plot contents and the two introductory artwork figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The decisive improvement is addressing the unsupported fixed-weight-to-uniform step in v1's central proof. Lemma A.1 and the new union-bound argument support appropriately revised guarantees, including corrected target-distribution quantifiers. Although the resulting bounds are weaker, their justification is materially stronger. The MCQA evaluation and more precise research positioning add useful support, despite sparse calibration details for the new experiment. Repairing the central theoretical argument constitutes a substantial overall quality gain.
